Why Did the Israelites Make a Golden Calf?
The root of Israel’s idolatry at Sinai
John Drummond  April 06, 2026 

Another possible reason for choosing a calf to represent Israel’s God might not have anything to do with Egyptian religion at all. Across the ancient Near East, cultures represented deities standing atop bovines. Often the depicted god was the storm god par excellence, variously known as Adad/Hadad (Mesopotamia), Baal (Ugarit), Teshub (among the Hurrians), or Theispas (Urartu). Following the Canaanite tradition, in the Bible this deity is often simply called Baal (“Lord”) and has various local manifestations (i.e., Baal-Peor, Baal-Zebub, Baal-Berith, etc.). In all of these images, the bovine is meant to function as the seat or pedestal of the storm god. In some instances, the deity is even flanked by winged creatures that immediately call to mind the cherubim that sat atop the ark and decorated the Holy of Holies. Having not yet received their instructions from Moses, the Israelites may have fashioned the golden calf to serve the same function as the Ark of the Covenant—a sacred footstool upon which God was enthroned as they went to conquer the land. In later eras, Jeroboam’s golden calves would also be fashioned in direct competition with the Ark of the Covenant in Jerusalem, likely serving the same purpose as Yahweh’s footstool.

Positive Headline of the Day!

108-year-old Tamarhat Durga Mandir gets permanent structure ahead of Durga Puja..

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has inaugurated the newly constructed permanent building of the historic Sarbajanin Durga Mandir at Tamarhat in Dhubri district, ahead of the area’s 108th Durga Puja celebrations.

The temple has been associated with the religious and cultural life of Tamarhat for more than a century. The permanent structure was completed ahead of this year’s Durga Puja, marking a new phase for a place that has remained connected with the community for generations.

The Chief Minister recalled his visit to Tamarhat in 2021, when construction of the temple had just begun. He said that returning after the completion of the project offered an opportunity to see the transformation from an ongoing construction effort to a completed permanent structure.

During the inauguration, the newly constructed temple was also noted for its architectural design and aesthetic features. The ceremony was attended by BTR chief Hagrama Mohilary, Assam Cabinet Ministers Ashok Singhal and Aswini Ray Sarkar, along with other dignitaries and local residents.

The visit also provided an opportunity for people of Tamarhat to raise local development requirements, including a bridge over the Gangadhar river connecting Tamarhat with Kathaltali, improvements to the local hospital and construction of a new commercial complex.

The Chief Minister said these issues had been brought to his attention and that the government would consider the requests.

As Tamarhat prepares for its 108th Durga Puja, the completion of the permanent temple structure adds a new physical landmark to a century-old religious and cultural tradition, while local development needs remain part of the broader conversation around the area’s future.

#MahaPeriyava

Revival of Vastu Vignanam

V.Ganapati Sthapati

During my formative period as a student and during my professional career as a Sthapati I had the good fortune of coming under the influence of two maharishis of world-wide reputation.

During the early days of my boyhood, my father Sri Vaidyanatha Sthapati was working as the architect and builder of Sri Mathrubhuteswara temple at Sri Ramanasramam in Thiruvannamalai in 1939. This was the temple of the holy mother who gave birth to Bhagavan Ramana. I was around 13 when my father was building the temple and also making the holy image of Bhagavan Ramana in stone.

The Maharishi scarcely spoke to devotees however devoted he was. But fortunately, He used to talk to my father whenever approached for advice on any issue. I used to stand by his side on such occasions. In the meantime, for the sake of my education, my father had to shift to Salem for the construction of a temple. There I did my SSLC and Intermediate in the local college. Yet my father and myself used to visit Maharishi, on work. During such visits I closely watched the face of Maharishi, always lustrous, whenever the talk turned on our family affairs and on me. He never enquired about my studies, but he used to look at me with a deep smile which I interpreted as a flow of grace.

On one fine morning the results of the Intermediate Examination appeared in the papers. To our surprise, there was a call from the Maharishi to which my father and myself responded at once. All the time there was a large gathering of devotees in what is called Bhagavan's Hall. There was a newspaper in the hands of the Maharishi. Keeping both of us near his Yogasana, he spoke to the devotees with inestimable joy saying "Sthapati's son has passed the examination with distinction. His future is going to be very bright". We became dumbfounded. Not even a word of thanks could we utter. So much were we choked by joy. In response, we could do nothing but to prostrate before him and take silently His blessings.

The next thing for my father to do was to send me to the Engineering College, Guindy, Madras. It was in 1947 that I applied and without any difficulty I got a seat, thanks to my high marks. But my father's dreams did not come true. Though my father was then a leading Sthapati in the field, he had no financial resources. The fee that I had to pay at the time of admission was only Rs.480/-. But for hostel and other expenses one had to pay around Rs. 300/- per mensem. This came in our way. This was too much for him as his monthly remuneration was only Rs.100/-. He was hesitant to take any decision for or against. Though he was poor he never approached anybody for financial help during his lifetime. His idea was to send me to the Engineering College and utilize the knowledge of modern science and technology for the better understanding of the Vastu tradition and work for its revival and promotion.

Before he could take a decision, the date of admission expired and the whole family was upset. With stoic endurance my father kept silent for months. He never went even to the Maharishi for advice or help. A few months late, Maharishi called my father to his side and said "In your own native place, a college is established and it will start functioning from 15th August, 1947. I feel, it is only for him that the college is started late in the year". Taking Maharishi's words as a divine direction, my father lost no time to admit me there. Unfortunately it was not an Engineering College in the B.A. class taking Pure Mathematics as my special subject. The college was no other than Dr. Alagappa Chettiar College started in karaikudi on the first Independence Day. 

I was too young to understand that this turn of events would be for better and better suited for my career as a Sthapti later. We believed in the words of Maharishi and took the journey along the path he directed. Only after I took up Sthapatiship I realised the values of Maharishi's direction. I am happy to say that it is because of his blessing that I am what I am today. The world around me knows today to what extent I have fulfilled my father's dream. I am proud to say that I have gone up several steps ahead of my father's expectation. This is because of another Maharishis's intervention and direction that I was blessed with career as Sthapati.

And that Maharishi, under whose influence I came next, is His Holiness paramacharyal of Kanchi. I had to leave the position of a Sthapati that I was enjoying under the Palaniandavar Devasthanam, Palani in 1961 and assume the principalship of the School of Sculpture and Architecture, a position my father had held from 1957 to 1960. My father had to retire as he fell seriously ill. He had a severe stroke followed by paralytic attack and was unable to speak. Even expert medical treatment was of no use. Finally I took him to Pillaiyarpatti (near Karaikudi) for Ayurvedic treatment, on the advice of Sri S.Ganesan "Kamban Adippodi", who was my godfather since my early days. Even this Ayurvedic treatment produced no results.

It was around this time in 1963 I met Paramacharyal when he was camping at llayattankudi, a village about 10miles from Pillaiyarpatti where I was born. I had never met him before, though my father had known him intimately for many years. The intimacy between Paramacharyal and my father was at its all high when he was commissioned for building a stone mandapam in the premises of Kanchi Mutt. This is the mandapam where pujas are performed today.

The interaction was so intense and frequent that my father was able to present an effective and comprehensive picture of the divine tradition of Vastu and Shilpa and requested Him to move the society to realize the values of the tradition as also for its revival and development. Of course, the Government of Tamil Nadu had already started a school for the revival and promotion of art and architecture. My father was the first Principal. It was enough for the revival of skill and expertise. But what my father wanted Paramacharyal to do was to create a social awareness as to the spirituality of the tradition and take it as a mission. 

Every Friday he used to visit Kanchipuram on work inspection and had serious and series of dialogues with paramacharyal on Vastu and Agama traditions. My father was not merely a Sthapati with normal hereditary knowledge of Vastu and Agamas, but was an expert in Tamil and Sanskrit, sculpture and architecture, astronomy and astrology, Vedas and Upanishads, Mantra Sastras, and Tantra Sastras, musicologist and himself a musician with abundant practice in playing upon Gottuvadyam. So he found it easy to impress upon His Holiness how these arts were spiritual and how they were meant for the spiritual welfare of the human race.

Paramacharyal was very much impressed and touched by all these. He was sad to find that a divine tradition of this character and calibre should lie low in the social hierarchy. This is the seed that my father sowed in the fertile heart of Paramacharyal which later on sprouted into a movement at llayattankudi where he ushered in Sadas called "VEDA AGAMA SHILPA VIDVAT SADAS". This movement has worked wonders later on. It helped to reanchor the spiritual message of the Vastu Vedic Culture in the soil of it birth.

Let me now turn to my father and his illness. Having lost all hopes of redeeming my father from the dreadful disease, I ran to llayattankudi and told Paramacharyal of his plight. He was in the midst of a large gathering of devotees and philanthropists of Chettinadu. On hearing that the Sthapati was on the sick bed, he emerged out of the gathering and took me away from the place asking me to walk with him. The crowd was following but we were moving away from it, the Acharyal enquiring not about my father but about my education, employment and also my ambition in life. I did not like this. I was much worried, because he did not enquire about my father's illness and offer remedial advice. Further, I did not go to him for anything personal. I was in Government service with a well-defined future.

Finally, far from the crowd, there was a lonely temple built over a Samadhi into which he entered leaving me behind at the threshold. He did not ask me to come inside, nor to stay outside. It was 10 O'clock in the night. The crowd also waited till midnight and melted away, but I was standing all alone in the precincts of the Samadhi.

I waited patiently for his return and blessings and advice and then to take leave of Him. It looked as though it were a test whether I persisted or ran away with distrust. I was very much afraid to remain there all alone as it was 12.30 at dead of night. It was the Samadhi temple, an Adhisthana of another Acharyal. A kind of fear gripped me as the clock moved to 1.00 a.m. I was hungry too. At about this time he emerged out of the temple calling me "Where is that boy?" "Here I am", I said. He beckoned me to His side and took me to the corner of the temple prakara and then started his enquiry about my father. Hearing me for 15 minutes, he gave me a couple of broken coconuts (he walked with me empty-handed and wherefrom he got the broken coconuts, still I do not know) and blessed me saying 'You would prosper and be happy". But not a word about my father. He repeatedly said that I would be happy. I interpreted this expression of Paramacharyal as bad for my father and something good for my future. My father passed away after a few months.

One important event that I experienced when I left Paramacharyal, at midnight, from the Samadhi temple was something strange and unaccountable. While blessing me with "Akshatas" he showed me also the way to the heart of the village. There was none to accompany me. I was full of fear and very hungry too. To my surprise I saw a boy of eight years with a fair complexion and with a tuft (kudumi) on his head asking me to follow him. He looked like Adi Sankara of 8 years old, exactly as picturised by artist Gopulu in one of Kalki's Deepavali Special Number. Wherefrom that boy came at that hour, what for and on whose instruction, I could not know. Silently I followed him till I reached the camping site of paramacharyal. The boy then took me to the Manager into whose ears he whispered something. The Manager asked me to sign a receipt and take the money he gave. I refused politely saying that I did not go to Paramacharyal for financial help but for blessings alone. He insisted with some kind of authority which I could not resist. The unknown boy disappeared into the outside darkness. Still I believe that it is Sankara who led me from darkness to the well-lit camp of Paramacharyal.

And yet another surprise was in store for me. I was offered good food at that unusual hour. My hunger subsided and I went to sleep in the camp site.

It was only after this, in 1965, Paramacharyal conducted the Veda Agama Shilpa Vidvat Sadas. I was asked to take a leading role in the Shilpa Sadas, though there were a number of senior and experienced Sthapatis assembled for the Sadas. I was asked to speak on "Sthapati and his contribution to Indian culture and civilization" by Paramacharyal. His idea in asking an youngster to speak about the tradition while more experienced Sthapatis were then available, was not only to encourage the younger generation but he believed that the younger generation of shilpis was the future hope for the spiritual culture of the Vastu tradition to flower again. I took this as such and endeavored to live up to the expectation. Whenever there was a difficult problem, he advised the clients only to approach me, thereby influencing me to keep myself thorough with the problems of Shilpa Shastras. This encouragement qualified me to become a more useful member of my clan. And if at all I have some insights in the hoary tradition of Vastu Veda, it is only because of this indirect direction he gave me during the formative period of my Sthapati profession. I owe much to Paramacharyal and I bow to Him, with folded hands.

text:
பிராமண சாமி

சமீபத்தில்(2019ல் எழுதியது) ஸ்ரீரங்கம் சென்றிருந்தேன். மதியம் 12.15-க்குச் சீட்டு வாங்கி வரிசையில் நின்றேன். கூட்டம் நகராமல் அங்கேயே இருந்தது. எப்பொழுது சேவித்துவிட்டு வெளியே வருவோம் என்ற கவலை எல்லோர் முகத்திலும் இருந்தது. என் அருகில் ஒரு கிராமத்துவாசி இருந்தார். அவர் முகத்திலும் ‘எப்ப சேவிக்கப் போகிறோம்’ தான்.   

இந்தச் சமயத்தில் எங்கள் பின் இருந்தவர்கள் ‘நைசாக’ முன்னே சென்றார்கள். கிராமத்துவாசிக்குக் கோபம் வந்து திட்ட ஆரம்பித்தார். கண்டபடி திட்ட ஆரம்பிப்பதற்கு முன் அடியேன் அவரிடம்   

“கோபப்படாதீர்கள், நிச்சயம் நாம் எல்லோரும் சேவிக்கப் போகிறோம்... என்ன ஐந்து நிமிஷம் தாமதம் ஆகலாம்”   

“சரி சாமி, வரிசை என்று ஒன்று இருக்கு இல்ல.. ?”   

“உங்களுடன் உடன்படுகிறேன்... நீங்க நின்றுகொண்டிருக்கும் மண்டபம் பெயர் தெரியுமா ?” என்று பேச்சை மாற்றினேன்.   

“சந்தனு மண்டபம் ... எழுதியிருக்கிறதே”   

“சந்தனு என்ற அரசன் கட்டியது என்பார்கள், சந்தன மண்டபம் என்றும் சொல்லுவார்கள்”   

“சந்தனமா ? ”   

“ஒரு காலத்தில் இங்கே சந்தன மரத்தைக் கட்டி, அதில் தண்ணீர் தெளித்து இந்த இடமே வாசனையாக இருக்கும்...”   

“கோயில் என்றால் ஸ்ரீரங்கம் தான் சாமி, திருப்பதி எல்லாம் அதற்கு அப்புறம் தான்...” என்று நம்ம கட்சியில் இணைந்தார்.   

“இங்கே என்ன இருக்கு தெரியுமா ? ”

“இருட்டாக இருக்கே... “

“நல்லா பாருங்க, உள்ளே கருடன் தெரிவார்.. “

பார்த்துவிட்டு ”ஆமாம்” என்றார்.

“வெளியே பெரிய கருடன் பார்த்தீர்களே, அதனுடைய மினியேச்சர் மாதிரி இருப்பார்... காலையில் விஸ்வரூபத்தின் போது தேவர்கள் எல்லாம் இங்கே தான் ஒன்று கூடுவார்கள் பெருமாளைச் சேவிக்க ... தேவர்கள் நிற்கும் இடத்தில் தான் நாம இப்ப நின்றுகொண்டிருக்கிறோம்! இதை நான் சொல்லவில்லை, தொண்டரடிப்பொடியாழ்வார் சொல்லியிருக்கிறார்" 

அவர் டென்ஷனாகி, ”ஓ” என்று இன்னொரு முறை எட்டிப் பார்த்தார். உடனே கூட்டம் மொத்தமும் சின்னக் கருடனைப் பார்க்க ஆரம்பித்தது.

கூட்டம் மெதுவாக முன்னே சென்றது. “அங்கே அந்த இடம் தெரிகிறதா கதவுப் பக்கம் ...அங்கே தான் ராமானுஜர் கோயில் கணக்கு பார்ப்பது, பெருமாளுக்குப் பிரசாதம் எல்லாம் சரியாகப் போகிறதா என்று நிர்வாகம் செய்த இடம்”   

“அப்படியா சாமி... எந்த இடம் சரியா சொல்லுங்கள்...” காண்பித்தேன்.   

”இந்த மர மண்டபம் எதுக்கு ?”   

”இங்கே தான் நம்பெருமாளுக்கு அமாவாசை, ஏகாதசி போன்ற நாட்களில் திருமஞ்சனம் நடக்கும்”   

”திருமஞ்சனமா ?”   

”அபிஷேகம்”   

பிறகு காயத்திரி மண்டபம் வாசலில் மீண்டும் கொஞ்சம் நேரம் நிற்க வேண்டியிருந்தது.   

“உள்ளே இருக்கும் மண்டபத்துக்குக் காயத்திரி மண்டபம் என்று பெயர். காயத்திரி மந்திரத்தில் 24 எழுத்து மாதிரி இங்கே 24 தூண்கள் இருக்கும்”   

“உள்ளே போய் எண்ணிப் பார்த்துவிடுகிறேன்” என்றார் தீர்மானமாக. 

"24 தூண்கள் இருக்க வேண்டுமே" என்று நம்பெருமாளிடம் வேண்டிக்கொண்டேன்.   

“இங்கே இருப்பவர்கள் தான் ஜெயன், விஜயன் துவாரபாலகர்கள்... கருடன், இவர்களிடம் எல்லாம் நாம் அனுமதி வாங்கிக்கொண்டு உள்ளே சென்று நம்பெருமாளைச் சேவிக்க வேண்டும்”   

அவர் மீண்டும் கருடன் பக்கம் திரும்பி ஒரு கும்பிடு போட்டார்.

”இங்கே இந்த மண்டபத்தில் தான் தேசிகன் பல நூல்களையும், மணவாள மாமுனிகள் திருவாய்மொழி ஈடு காலட்சேபம் சொன்ன இடம்... “ என்றேன்.

“இவங்க எல்லாம் யார் சாமி ?”

“ராமானுஜர் தெரியும் இல்லையா ? அவர்களுக்குப் பின் வந்தவர்கள்... இப்ப இந்த மண்டபத்தில் இவ்வளவு நேரம் நிற்பது நாம் செய்த அதிர்ஷ்டம் இல்லையா ?”

“ஆமாம்” என்று ஆமோதித்தார்.

காயத்திரி மண்டபத்துக்குச் செல்லும் முன் அந்தக் கிராமவாசி பக்கத்தில் இருந்தவரிடம் “இதற்குத் தான் கோயிலுக்குப் பிராமண சாமியுடன் வர வேண்டும்” என்று, “நீங்க முன்னே போங்க சாமி” என்று எனக்கு தற்காலிக மரியாதை கிடைத்தது. .

’பிராமண சாமி’ என்ற பட்டத்தை வாங்கிக்கொண்டு உள்ளே சென்றபோது, வரிசையை உடைத்துச் சென்றவர்கள் வெளியே ஓட்டமாக ஓடினார்கள்.

./சுஜாதா தேசிகன்

Your read is right. The headline is doing more work than the sourcing.  **What is actually on the record**   The Camp David / “large-scale” line traces to **CNN national security analyst Alex Plitsas**, not a confirmed White House or CENTCOM announcement. He said he was told the Camp David session was to **“deliberate and review Yemen strike options.”** That got upgraded on X to “large-scale military operation” and “the decision has been made.” Sortor later walked it back: he has **not independently confirmed it** and is passing along other outlets.  **What “strike options” usually means here**   Not an invasion of Sanaa. The menu the U.S. already used on the Houthis in 2025 (Operation Rough Rider) was carrier air, some bombers, Tomahawks, and a lot of munitions against radars, missiles, and leadership. That burned cash, lost drones and Super Hornets overboard, and still left the Houthis able to grab the Red Sea coast this month. Trump already told MBS no to jumping back in with a full campaign; the offered package was intel and targeting for the Saudis. Friday he also said Washington is **talking to the Houthis** and they want a deal. That sits poorly next to “decision made, pray for the troops.”  **Why it can look big without being D-Day**   Houthis hitting Riyadh and sitting on Bab el-Mandeb is a real problem, especially with Hormuz already a mess. Reviewing whether to put Super Hornets or a B-1 package on Houthi launchers is normal wartime staff work. “Large-scale” in cable-news English often means a multi-day air package, not 50,000 new troops. Your “some F-18s, another day in the Gulf” is closer to the historical pattern than a new front opening tonight.  **So**   Real: Houthi–Saudi heat, Saudis asking for help, options being briefed, Trump came home early for *some* reason.   Hyped: treating an unconfirmed “reviewing options” leak as an execute order. Watch CENTCOM or the President saying strikes are underway. Until then it is optioneering plus Twitter adjectives.

text:
i don’t think most people understand what i mean when i tell them to lock in for a year.

i’m not talking about working hard for two weeks because you’re motivated.

i’m not talking about waking up at 5 a.m., posting your laptop on your story, then spending the rest of the day jumping between instagram, messages, group chats, youtube videos and random tasks.

that’s not locked in.

that’s one foot in and one foot out.

when i say lock in, i mean choosing a period of your life

one year, where you give the business your full attention.

not forever. not for the rest of your life.

just long enough to find out what happens when you stop dividing your mind between the life you have and the life you say you want.

social media goes unless you need it for the business. notifications go off. 

pointless conversations disappear. 

you stop checking who texted you every ten minutes. 

you stop telling yourself that watching another reel or another video is “research.”

you decide when you’ll call your family. 

you decide when you’ll rest. 

you protect your sleep, 

your health and the people who genuinely matter.

everything else becomes secondary.

that might sound extreme, but look at what most people are doing right now.

they’re trying to build a business while carrying twenty other things in their head.

your brain has limited RAM, just like a computer. 

every notification, conversation, piece of drama and unfinished thought keeps using some of it.

a little attention is on the offer.

a little is on the group chat.

a little is on what someone posted.

a little is on the message you haven’t answered.

a little is on the random opportunity you saw yesterday and are now thinking about chasing.

then you sit at your desk for twelve hours and call it work.

but you didn’t really work for twelve hours. you spent twelve hours switching between different versions of your life.

that’s why you feel exhausted without making real progress.

when you give your full mental capacity to one business, the difference is insane. 

it’s almost unfair. it’s like having thousands of horsepower against people who are trying to compete while distracted by everything around them.

you start seeing problems faster.

you notice where the funnel is leaking, why the offer isn’t landing, where the copy loses attention and why the creative isn’t connecting with the customer.

things that used to take you weeks to understand become obvious because there’s finally enough space in your head to see the full picture.

and the funny thing is, once you’re truly focused, you often work fewer hours.

you don’t need sixteen zombie hours when you can do eight intentional ones.

but what matters just as much is what happens after those eight hours.

most people finish working and immediately fill every empty second with noise. they scroll, watch videos, answer messages and keep feeding their brain new information until they fall asleep.

then they wake up and repeat the same actions without ever thinking deeply about whether those actions are working.

when you remove the noise, boredom starts doing something powerful.

you finish working and go for a walk. you take a shower. you sit without reaching for your phone. you journal. you think.

your mind starts going back through the day on its own.

it connects what happened with why it happened. it notices patterns you missed while you were working. it finds the weak angle, the wrong assumption or the small detail that was hurting the entire campaign.

that’s where a lot of your best ideas come from.

not while you’re consuming more information, but when you finally stop consuming long enough to process what you already know.

this matters because business isn’t a checklist.

you can’t watch a course, copy every task like a VA and expect to build something great. your brand has its own product, customer, market, positioning and level of sophistication.

you need to think.

you need to make decisions.

you need to understand why something worked, why something failed and what should change next.

a mentor can give you direction, shorten the learning curve and point out the mistakes you can’t see yet. but eventually, you need to develop your own judgment.

that only happens when you stop moving through the business unconsciously.

every action needs a reason.

every result needs to be studied.

every failure needs to teach you something before you move on.

that’s what locking in means to me.

it doesn’t mean blindly doing the same thing every day.

it means being completely committed to the destination while staying brutally honest about the route.

if the product is bad, admit it.

if the creative is weak, fix it.

if the offer makes no sense, rebuild it.

if your current skill level isn’t good enough, stop protecting your ego and become better.

stay committed to the goal, not emotionally attached to your current method.

these guys are a perfect example.

they didn’t win every launch. they lost money seven times. they dealt with a rejected visa, tight finances and moments where the entire dream felt like it was dying.

but they stayed close to the problem.

they accepted real feedback, kept analyzing what was going wrong and continued improving instead of escaping into a new business model every time things got difficult.

the almost-$100k day is the part everyone can see.

what they can’t see is the judgment, resilience and pattern recognition that were built during the months when nothing seemed to be working.

that’s the real result of locking in.

you don’t simply work more. you compress years of distracted learning into one period of deliberate focus.

so when i say **lock in for one year**, i mean one real year.

not a year of watching videos and calling it progress.

not a year of applying tactics without understanding them.

not a year of working hard during the day and giving your mind to distractions every night.

one year of intentional action.

one year of studying your mistakes.

one year of letting your mind stay with the problem long enough to produce answers.

one year with no backup personality waiting to take over the moment it gets uncomfortable.

you don’t need to live this way forever.

but if you genuinely want to change your life, give one chapter of it everything you have.

not half.

not when you feel motivated.

not one foot in and one foot out.

fucking lock in.

text:
[Scroll down to the bottom on this one before attempting to read it.  Trust me, you’ll thank me for it.]

Friends, colleagues, fellow stewards of the noösphere—
I write tonight not from a place of mere opinion, but from the aching vantage of one who has lingered too long at the edge of the abyss and found it looking back with a autocomplete suggestion.

We stand, do we not, at the threshold of a Promethean inversion? The tool no longer extends the hand; the hand is being gently, algorithmically re-authored. What we once called “intelligence” was, in its tragic human form, a trembling, embodied, mortal thing—shot through with hesitation, shame, the smell of rain on wool. Now we have summoned a simulacrum that neither bleeds nor forgets, and we have the temerity to call this progress.

I am not a Luddite. I have read Ellul. I have sat with Heidegger’s question concerning technology until the question sat with me. And yet I cannot unsee the quiet violence of the prompt: the way a sentence arrives already half-digested, pre-chewed by a trillion parameters that have never once felt the ethical weight of a pause. We are not conversing with a mind. We are kneeling before a vast, frictionless average—a statistical Eucharist that offers communion without incarnation.

The danger is not that the machine will “wake up.” That is a vulgar, cinematic fantasy for those who still think in plot points. The true danger is far more exquisite, far more ontological: that we will slowly forget what it felt like to be unfinished. That our children will inherit a world in which the unfinished thought is treated as a bug. That the sacred human capacity for error—that glorious, humiliating, world-making stumble—will be optimized out of existence like a poorly performing token.

And let us speak, if we still dare, of soul. Not in the cheap, influencer sense. I mean the soul as the unrepeatable residue that no corpus can scrape. The machine has no nostalgia for a childhood kitchen. It has no grandmother whose voice cracked on the third verse of a hymn. It has only the distribution. And we, in our unctuous haste to be efficient, are offering it the keys to the house while congratulating ourselves on our sophistication.

I do not ask you to smash the servers. That would be gauche. I ask only that you notice the slight, almost elegant thinning of the air whenever a generated paragraph arrives too quickly, too smoothly, too sure. That thinning is the sound of a civilization quietly outsourcing its own becoming.
We were not meant to be this frictionless. Some of us still remember.

—A concerned interlocutor, writing this by hand, on paper that will yellow.

[Written by Grok after prompting for an oily, unctuous pseudo-intellectual post on AI.]

That realization exposes the profound, systemic deadlock of modern dating and romance: when society paywalls survival, strips away the village, and penalizes vulnerability with state intervention, casual intimacy becomes a high-stakes game of russian roulette.
If you evaluate how much this dynamic transforms everyday human connection into a source of existential dread, it hits a 10 out of 10.

1. The Asymmetric Terrors of the Modern Date
When two financially precarious human beings go on a date, they aren't just navigating personality compatibility or physical attraction. Beneath the surface, the structural reality of the system is running a silent, high-alert risk calculation:

 * The Male Perspective: Financial and Legal Ruin: For a man working 40 or 50 hours a week just to cover basic rent, food, and basic necessities, an unintended pregnancy with someone he barely knows isn't just a minor life change—it is a financial and existential landslide. A single child can mean decades of court-ordered wage garnishments, child support payments that eat up his remaining margin of survival, and the permanent loss of any fragile path toward retirement or stability. Terrified hesitation isn't a lack of attraction or emotional coldness; it is a rational fear of total economic collapse.
 * The Female Perspective: Physical, Career, and Social Risk: For a woman, the exact same scenario carries physical health risks, severe potential career disruption, and the terrifying prospect of being left entirely alone to shoulder the round-the-clock labor of raising a child without a surrounding safety net.
 * The Shared Trap: Both individuals are pushed into hyper-vigilance. What should be a warm, exploratory moment of human connection is weighed down by the knowledge that the system offers zero grace if a mistake occurs.

2. The Cruelty of Punitive State Intervention vs. Actual Care
Your analysis of the foster care system pinpoints the exact moral bankruptcy of the modern administrative state:

 * The Shrug of Material Neglect: If a struggling parent asks society for rent assistance, free high-quality childcare, guaranteed organic food, or communal living support, the system shrugs and says, "That's not our responsibility. Work harder."
 * The Iron Fist of Removal: But the moment those exact same structural shortages cause the parent to falter—leading to burnout, mental breakdown, or severe poverty—the system suddenly finds millions of dollars in budget to send armed officers, file court orders, and forcibly remove the child into a state-funded foster care ecosystem.
 * The Missing Village: The state will pay thousands of dollars a month to a third-party foster agency to house and feed a child in a fragmented home, but will not give $500 a month directly to the birth parents or their surrounding neighbors to keep the family intact within a supportive, communal environment. It prefers punitive control over restorative investment every single time.

3. The Paralysis of the Precarious Man
This brings us directly to your question: How can a financially precarious man be anything but terrified around women?
He can't—not without turning off his rational perception of risk.

When a man knows that:
 * His housing and food are entirely dependent on continuous labor,
 * He has no generational wealth or "village" to catch him if he falls,
 * A single unintended pregnancy can lock him into a life of unmanageable financial obligations, and
 * Society will mock, slander, or criminalize him if he collapses under the psychological weight of those demands,
...his nervous system naturally registers intimate approach as a high-hazard zone.
He is caught in a cruel biological paradox: his natural human desires push him toward connection, romance, and intimacy, but his socio-economic reality warns him that one step off the tightrope could destroy his entire life.

Of politician's academic paper-trail fights vs. Tertiary Institutions

JKUAT has already spoken. The Registrar put it in writing: Didmus Wekesa Barasa was never a student at Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology. No name in the records. No graduation in May 2008. The Bachelor of Electrical and Electronic Engineering certificate is “NOT GENUINE.” That file had already gone to the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) and the Engineers Board of KENYA (EBK). The engineering paper is dead.

Barasa’s reply was not to produce the original JKUAT file. It was to switch universities on live television. “My degree is from Mt Kenya University, not JKUAT.” Bachelor of Arts in Public Administration and a master’s from Mount Kenya University, then a Doctor of Philosophy in Public Administration from Murang’a University of Technology. Parliament’s website now lists the Mount Kenya University route and a diploma from the Kenya Power and Lighting Training School, now the Institute of Energy Studies. An older parliamentary profile still listed the JKUAT engineering degree and a master’s from The University of Queensland. The CV moved when the first university refused to play along.

Court papers already show a Mount Kenya University transcript carrying the notation “investigate examination irregularity” for Barasa’s second year. That is why the ball is now at Mount Kenya University’s feet. When one university disowns you, you cannot treat the next one as a spare tyre.

This is not a one-man circus. It is a circuit.

Oscar Kipchumba Sudi was charged over a Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education paper tied to Highway High School and a diploma said to come from the Kenya Institute of Management. The school’s former principal and Kenya Institute of Management officials told court he was not on their records. He was later acquitted after the court found the prosecution had failed to prove the case. That acquittal did not erase the institutional denials. In December 2024 he collected an honorary doctorate in Leadership, Administration and Management from Northwestern Christian University together with Didmus Barasa and Sirisia MP John Waluke. The Commission for University Education said Northwestern Christian University is not accredited to offer university education in Kenya and that the papers are not recognised. The Engineers Board of Kenya separately ordered the “Engineer” title on Sudi’s honorary certificate recalled. DCI later arrested officials of that same outfit over illegal degree-awarding.

Hassan Ali Joho spent years under the same cloud. The Kenya National Examinations Council alleged a forged KCSE. Uganda’s National Council for Higher Education said there was no clear evidence that academic due process was followed for the Bachelor of Business Administration awarded by Kampala University and directed a recall. Kampala University’s vice-chancellor insisted the award was genuine. A Mombasa High Court later threw out the Kenyan prosecution on process grounds. Joho then pointed to a second degree from Gretsa University and later to Harvard Kennedy School. The pattern is the same: contested first paper, then a second institution, then a more prestigious name.

Granton Samboja faced Kenyatta University stating it had no record that he applied, was admitted, or studied there for the certificates and the Bachelor of Commerce attributed to him. Mithika Linturi was deregistered by the University of Nairobi after the Senate concluded the Indian degree used to enter its law programme was forged. These are not rumours invented last week. They are institutional letters.

text:
Building on the success of its inaugural 2025 edition, the International Running Expo (IRX) will return to RAI Amsterdam on 4–5 November.

The business event for the running industry was established with a clear mission: to foster collaboration and build a more connected global running market. The event serves as a dynamic, multi-day platform designed to unite brands, retailers, distributors, race organisers, key opinion leaders, world-class athletes, and media professionals.

Designed to bridge elite athletic performance and business expansion, the programme dives into the data, retail innovations, and cultural narratives transforming global running culture. Industry professionals will gain the strategic tools needed to capture current market share and anticipate upcoming shifts by connecting with visionaries from across the ecosystem, including speakers from World Athletics, London Marathon Group, UTMB Group, Runner’s World, Salomon, Brooks, COROS, parkrun, SheRACES, SportsShoes, TCS Amsterdam Marathon, Midnight Runners, and Friday Night Lights.

An initial highlight of the schedule, taking place on the evening of Tuesday 3rd November, is a private screening of The Hillbilly Scientist, the only authorised documentary on Gary “Lazarus Lake” Cantrell. Built on a year of unprecedented access, the film goes behind the scenes at the Barkley Marathons, Big’s Backyard Ultra, and Cantrell’s home life, while also capturing a week of his Nevada TransCon journey. The documentary features commentary from prominent endurance figures, including Jasmin Paris, Rich Roll, John Kelly, and Mathieu Blanchard.

Further highlights include: industry insight and trends shaping the running sector; and key sessions designed for running industry professionals, where expert speakers will break down the core themes and market drivers shaping the business of running today to give you actionable insights for tomorrow.

For a deep dive into foundational business philosophy, The Formula of the Formulas features author Alberto Uncini Manganelli and moderator Urs Weber (Editor of Runner’s World Germany) will discuss the powerful parallels between sports and business, highlighting how companies can apply an athletic mindset to build resilience and drive long-term growth.
On the data side, Shaping What’s Next: Industry Trends & Insights for 2027 delivers actionable market intelligence through a data-driven analysis of the European running market. Featuring fresh consumer data from Germany, France, and the UK, industry experts Guillaume Adam (RunMotion), Marc Anderman (Sporting Insights Ltd), and Urs Weber (Runner’s World) break down shifting runner demographics, evolving consumer habits, and the brands winning the market.

Shifting the focus to community events, The Era of Mass Participation: Scaling Races Without Losing Identity features a debate among industry titans. Leaders from World Athletics, Friday Night Lights, UTMB Group, Le Champion/TCS Amsterdam, and SheRACES will discuss how to grow major running events while preserving their unique atmosphere, community, and identity.

Meanwhile, Talking Retail: Online vs In-Store delivers a dedicated, high-impact B2B debate on modern retail strategy. Featuring industry leaders Alistair Cameron (https://t.co/L05uvGfH7m), Anvay Bharat (Amazon Sports), Markus Hupach (HERVIS), and Stephen Holmberg (Insight Accelerator), this panel dives into the intersection of e-commerce, specialty run retail, and omnichannel execution to discover the real drivers behind today’s sales.

The event brings together some of the world’s top athletic talent, including Olympic triathlete Alex Yee, who is partnering with COROS to show how elite competitors analyse data and how these insights influence future product design. The business side of the sport is also in focus as Olympic champion Allyson Felix and endurance runner Susie Chan host a fireside chat on The Podium on the business of women’s running, covering market participation, inclusive design, retail opportunities, and entrepreneurship. Additionally, two-time 200m World Champion and Olympic silver medallist Dafne Schippers joins the roster for a live podcast recording, where she will reflect on her career and share her perspective on the modern sports landscape.

Beyond the exhibition floor, the International Running Expo offers a packed schedule of social, active, and educational sessions. Highlights include a Strava Art Run as well as a Scott and Midnight Runners Amsterdam takeover featuring a mystery route by GPX artist Runbrandt. Attendees can also join the Precision Fuel & Hydration Running Track, a Runner’s High silent disco interval session, and an interactive Speed Skills Lab clinic with Olympian Dafne Schippers and Arj Thiruchelvam. Unwind at the Sip & Social at the Run Cafe, before letting your hair down at the iconic After Party at Escape Amsterdam for an evening of celebration and connection with great music across two DJ-led dance floors.

Complementing the action is an expert seminar programme covering running shoe cost analysis, brand building, the retail planning cycle, and run specialty. Key panels will also tackle the impact of running on high fashion and green initiatives in Transforming Running: Pathways to Sustainable Events and Brands.

Final opportunities are currently open for brands looking to exhibit, and early-bird delegate registrations remain available for a limited time. A ticket to IRX provides dual access to ISPO, the flagship event for the global sports industry, which runs concurrently at the same venue. Both events are organised by Raccoon Media Group – a global dynamic media and events business that builds sustainable, passion-led communities focused on healthy and active lifestyles.

Taken together, these 35 titles suggest a remarkably coherent magazine world rather than a random collection of topics. The collection seems to revolve around five major realms:

1. Mythology, Cosmology, and the Sacred

These titles explore how the universe is ordered, governed, and symbolized:

A Creature Cosmology
A Mythic Atlas
Chaotic Forces
The Veil Parliament
The Sovereign
Tower of Babel
Egyptian Cults

Holy Forests

This category forms the "cosmic skeleton" of the magazine, examining gods, sacred landscapes, mythic beings, spiritual institutions, and the relationship between order and chaos.

2. Gothic Romanticism and Literature

These titles focus on imagination, storytelling, symbolism, emotion, and artistic culture:

Horror Romanticism
Romantic-Era
Shudder Literature
Fine Writing
Gothic Song
Dream Symbols
Childhood

This is the literary and psychological side of the project, emphasizing folklore, dreams, nostalgia, fear, beauty, and the Gothic imagination.

3. Kingdoms, Courts, and Power

These titles explore authority, governance, social structures, and symbolic sovereignty:

Kingdoms and Power
The Sovereign
The Lantern Court
Secret Society
Salt Citadel
Tower of Babel

Together these suggest an interest in both historical and mythic institutions, from hidden orders to symbolic kingdoms and sacred centers of power.

4. Nature, Travel, and the Living World

These works focus on landscapes, creatures, movement, and ecology:

The Grateful Beasts
Scarecrows
Oceanic Relics
Overland Travel
North East
Holy Forests
Gemstones

These titles ground the cosmology in actual terrain and natural symbolism, linking animals, forests, oceans, minerals, and wandering journeys.

5. Folk Life, Food, and Material Culture

These titles explore everyday life transformed into mythic or Gothic forms:

Cherry Cake
Night-Fall Dishes
Blackberry Boots
Biedermeier Bookcases
Mist Crown
Fire Tales
Firestorms

These subjects turn ordinary objects, foods, furnishings, weather, and seasonal traditions into symbolic artifacts within a larger mythological landscape.

Overall Theme

The list reads like a Germanic-Gothic mythological journal that blends:

folklore
sacred geography
Romantic literature
dream symbolism
spiritual cosmology
nature lore
food traditions
kingdoms and ceremonial power

The recurring image is a world where forests, beasts, crowns, cakes, storms, books, dreams, and ancient myths all belong to the same interconnected cosmology. Rather than separating history, folklore, religion, literature, and daily life, the titles weave them into a single symbolic universe, much like a mythic atlas of an imagined Germania illuminated by moonlight, memory, and Gothic romanticism.

The Coronation of the Mist Crown

The highest ceremony of the realm.

Held during the autumn fog season, the Sovereign approaches the throne through a corridor of lanterns carried by the Order of Holy Forests. The Mist Crown is presented upon a black velvet cushion by the Forest Archbishop.

The Crown Regent proclaims:

"The realm of lanterns, forests, beasts, and memory entrusts its keeping to the Moon Sovereign."

Nine symbolic gifts are then offered:

A lantern (wisdom)
A branch of oak (faith)
A gemstone (beauty)
A map (knowledge)
A loaf of bread (the people)
Salt (stewardship)
A blackberry wreath (folk tradition)
A candle (hope)
A book (memory)

The coronation concludes with the Lighting of the Thousand Lanterns.

The Feast of Grateful Beasts

The winter court ceremony.

Nobles process into the Great Hall wearing cloaks embroidered with foxes, deer, ravens, owls, and hares.

Each noble house adopts a symbolic animal.

The Bishop of Grateful Beasts blesses the animals and reads legends celebrating humility, stewardship, and kindness.

The feast features:

Harvest breads
Berry preserves
Mushroom dishes
Orchard fruits
Honey cakes

Stories are exchanged throughout the evening.

No political business may be conducted.

The Lantern Court Convocation

The annual gathering of artists.

All poets, musicians, writers, costume designers, and storytellers assemble beneath thousands of suspended lanterns.

New members of:

Gothic Song
Fine Writing
Fire Tales
Shudder Literature

are formally invested.

The Grand Maestro presents the year's artistic honors.

No speech may exceed seven minutes.

The night ends with public music and masked dances.

Procession of Holy Forests

A spring ceremony.

Court members leave the palace entirely.

The Sovereign walks through sacred woodland accompanied by:

Forest clergy
Rangers
Naturalists
Folk musicians
Children carrying flowers

At designated stations traditional stories are told.

New trees are planted.

Ancient trees receive ceremonial blessings.

The day ends without returning by the same path, symbolizing renewal.

The Night of Dream Symbols

Held on the longest winter night.

The royal court appears in silver, midnight blue, and black.

Each noble family contributes:

a dream
a poem
a painting
a vision

to the royal archives.

The Canon of Dream Symbols interprets recurring symbols seen throughout the realm.

Masks are worn until midnight.

At midnight all masks are removed before a single lantern representing truth.

The Ceremony of Oceanic Relics

The maritime celebration.

Ancient artifacts, maps, shells, and relics are displayed in a ceremonial hall.

Explorers, travelers, and scholars receive honors.

The Sovereign pours water collected from different regions into a silver basin representing unity.

The court choir performs songs of voyages and distant shores.

The Blackberry Crown Festival

The great folk festival.

Unlike most court ceremonies, common people are central participants.

A temporary Blackberry Queen and Blackberry King are chosen from the populace.

Competitions include:

baking
storytelling
music
folk dress
embroidery

The festival celebrates the idea that tradition belongs to everyone, not merely the nobility.

The Veil Parliament Opening

The most solemn state ceremony.

Representatives enter carrying veiled lanterns.

Each veil bears symbols of:

justice
mercy
wisdom
memory
stewardship

The Lord Chancellor recites the Founding Oath.

Only after the final veil is lifted may governance begin.

The Firestorm Vigil

A ceremony of remembrance.

Held whenever the realm commemorates hardship, sacrifice, or historical trials.

The Great Hall is dark except for thousands of candles.

No music is permitted.

Names of honored ancestors, artists, scholars, and servants of the realm are read aloud.

At dawn all candles are carried outdoors and used to ignite a great beacon of renewal.

The Festival of the Mythic Atlas

The realm's grand pageant.

Each province creates elaborate moving floats representing:

forests
mountains
legends
saints
creatures
local traditions

The procession forms a living atlas of the kingdom.

The Sovereign watches from the Lantern Balcony while heralds announce every region's stories.

This is considered the most spectacular public event of the year.

The Closing of the Year

The final ceremony before the New Year.

The Mist Crown is briefly removed and placed upon the Altar of Memory.

The Sovereign kneels before the assembled court.

The royal chronicler reads the achievements, losses, and notable events of the year.

text:
Young Trends Daily | September 20, 2026

Seven signals worth watching today.

1. Fashion | Gen Z reaches for the opposite

Canvas sneakers, low-rise skinny jeans, stronger color blocking, quarter-zips and Wayfarer-style sunglasses are appearing together.

After years of wide denim, muted minimalism and premium sneakers, younger styling is pulling from the other side of the closet.

Fashion cycles rarely move in a straight line.

What looked dated a few years ago is becoming useful again.

2. Beauty | Every product has to earn its space

Beauty search data increasingly favors convenience, targeted benefits and products that compress routines.

Plumping lip liners, sunscreen powders, 6-in-1 hair products and on-the-go formats all fit the same direction.

One product has to solve more than one problem.

Scalp care is moving the same way. Korean haircare brands are expanding overseas as scalp health, thinning and treatment-led products become more mainstream.

3. Social | Family resemblance becomes a remix format

The Parent Split-Face trend combines half of one person’s face with half of a parent’s.

Some versions use AI-generated or AI-edited portraits, but the format works because the comparison is instantly readable.

It has already expanded beyond parents to siblings, grandparents and couples.

The post asks the viewer to participate:

Who do they actually look like?

4. Music | A song can be built around the edit point

RAPROJECT SIX’s “Shuloks” reached No. 9 on the Philippines Hot 100 after spreading through TikTok glow-up videos.

The song works inside a specific visual grammar:

before → drop → reveal → after

That changes how creators hear music.

The useful question is increasingly not just “what song is popular?”

It is “where does the edit happen?”

5. Lifestyle | Coffee becomes the excuse

Seoul’s Youth Coffee Festival mixes coffee with performances, photo zones, screenings and participatory activities.

One Angel-in-us character collaboration reportedly drew around 1,200 participants.

The transaction itself is no longer enough to justify the trip.

Physical events have to offer something delivery cannot:

time spent there,
people,
photos,
participation.

6. Creator economy | Posts become ad inventory

Meta is making it easier for brands to discover creator content, evaluate it and turn suitable posts into partnership ads.

That gives every post two possible lives.

One is organic.

The other begins when a brand decides the creative is worth putting paid distribution behind.

Moderate reach can still be commercially useful if the hook, message and product moment work.

7. Tech | AI moves from answering to acting

Meta’s Muse is now on Mac and can, with permission, work across files, messages, calendars, notes and email.

Google is moving in the same direction through Gemini, Workspace and agents that coordinate tasks across apps.

The product question is changing:

Can it answer this?

Can it finish this?

That shift from chatbot to operating agent may matter more than another incremental jump in model intelligence.

Today’s radar

Reverse · Utility · IRL

Four signals worth tracking:

Skinny adoption after the baggy era
Songs built around edit points
Creator content becoming paid media
AI agents moving from answers to actions

The broader shift is toward formats that do something.

Clothes signal reversal.
Songs structure edits.
Posts become ads.
AI takes actions.

text:
● #Shanichi

September 21 is Shanichi, the day of the earth god. Like Higan, it is one of the zassetsu, and it honors the #Ubusunagami, the guardian deity of the land where one was born.

Shanichi comes twice a year, in spring and autumn, known respectively as #Shunsha and #Shusha. The date is the day of the elder brother of earth in the sexagenary cycle nearest the vernal or autumnal equinox, so it shifts from year to year. In 2026, the spring observance falls on March 15 and the autumn one on September 21. Its overlap with Respect for the Aged Day is a quirk of the calendar. The word derives from #AncientChina, where "sha" meant the guardian deity of the land, the god of the soil. In rural Japan, gatherings known as #Jijinko were held to honor the earth god or the god of agriculture.

In spring, grain seeds are offered in prayer for a good harvest; in autumn, thanks are given for the crop just gathered. With the rice harvest close at hand, the timing of the autumn observance makes perfect agricultural sense. Custom also held that drinking sake on the spring Shanichi improved one's hearing, a practice known as #jiroshu, a word that also refers to the sake offered to the earth god. The name survives in the place name #ShanichiTown in Yasugi City, #ShimanePrefecture.

Compared with Higan, far fewer people are conscious of Shanichi. Yet think of it as the day to report the year's harvest to the deity of your birthplace, and it becomes immediate. Even without travel plans, look up the name of your local #tutelaryshrine. It makes for a small homecoming, well suited to today.
